subject: Introduction to Mechanical Engineering
title: Thermal and Energy Systems — MCQ Practice
note: Original ACADRIX practice MCQs based on the R-2025 Unit III scope and existing ACADRIX question bank. Not official university questions or verified PYQs.

questions.q: A thermodynamic system is best described as:
options: A specified quantity of matter or region in space selected for study
Only the surroundings of a machine
questions.answer: A specified quantity of matter or region in space selected for study
questions.explanation: A thermodynamic system is the matter or region selected for thermodynamic analysis.

questions.q: Everything external to the system that can interact with it is called the:
questions.answer: Surroundings
questions.explanation: The surroundings comprise everything external to the system that may interact with it.

questions.q: A closed system permits transfer of:
options: Energy but not mass across its boundary
Mass only when pressure is constant
questions.answer: Energy but not mass across its boundary
questions.explanation: In a closed system, mass remains fixed while energy may cross the boundary as heat and/or work.

questions.q: An open system permits transfer of:
options: Mass and energy across its boundary
Energy only with no mass transfer
Mass only with no energy transfer
questions.answer: Mass and energy across its boundary
questions.explanation: An open system, or control volume, can exchange both mass and energy with its surroundings.

questions.q: An isolated system ideally permits transfer of:
questions.answer: Neither mass nor energy
questions.explanation: An isolated system has no transfer of mass or energy across its boundary.

questions.q: Heat transfer occurs because of a difference in:
questions.answer: Temperature
questions.explanation: Heat spontaneously transfers due to a temperature difference between interacting bodies or regions.

questions.q: Work is classified as:
options: A property stored in a system
An energy transfer associated with a generalized force and displacement
questions.answer: An energy transfer associated with a generalized force and displacement
questions.explanation: Work is energy in transit associated with force-displacement or analogous interactions across a system boundary.

questions.q: Fourier's law is associated with:
questions.answer: Conduction heat transfer
questions.explanation: Fourier's law relates conductive heat transfer to the temperature gradient and thermal conductivity.

questions.q: For one-dimensional conduction through a plane wall, increasing thermal conductivity generally:
options: Reduces heat transfer for a given temperature gradient
Increases heat transfer for a given temperature gradient
questions.answer: Increases heat transfer for a given temperature gradient
questions.explanation: Higher thermal conductivity permits a greater conductive heat-transfer rate for the same temperature gradient and geometry.

questions.q: Convection heat transfer involves heat transfer between a surface and:
questions.answer: A moving or flowing fluid
questions.explanation: Convection involves energy transfer between a surface and an adjacent fluid, with fluid motion contributing to the process.

questions.q: Newton's law of cooling is commonly used for:
questions.answer: Convective heat transfer
questions.explanation: Newton's cooling relation expresses convective heat transfer using a heat-transfer coefficient and surface-to-fluid temperature difference.

questions.q: Natural convection is driven mainly by:
questions.answer: Buoyancy caused by density differences
questions.explanation: Natural convection results from buoyancy forces arising from density variations caused by temperature differences.

questions.q: Forced convection requires:
options: A phase change in every case
questions.answer: An externally imposed fluid motion
questions.explanation: Forced convection uses devices or pressure differences, such as fans or pumps, to drive fluid motion.

questions.q: Thermal radiation can transfer energy through:
questions.answer: A vacuum
questions.explanation: Radiation does not require a material medium and can propagate through vacuum.

questions.q: A blackbody is an ideal surface that:
options: Absorbs all incident radiation at all wavelengths
questions.answer: Absorbs all incident radiation at all wavelengths
questions.explanation: An ideal blackbody has absorptivity equal to one and is also the maximum possible emitter at a given temperature.

questions.q: Emissivity of a real surface is a measure of its radiation emission relative to:
options: An ideal blackbody at the same temperature
questions.answer: An ideal blackbody at the same temperature
questions.explanation: Emissivity compares radiation emitted by a real surface with that of a blackbody under the same conditions.

questions.q: The Stefan–Boltzmann law relates blackbody radiation to:
options: Absolute temperature to the fourth power
Absolute temperature only to the first power
questions.answer: Absolute temperature to the fourth power
questions.explanation: Blackbody emissive power is proportional to T⁴, according to the Stefan–Boltzmann law.

questions.q: Which heat-transfer mode can occur without bulk fluid motion and without electromagnetic emission across a vacuum?
questions.answer: Conduction
questions.explanation: Conduction transfers energy through microscopic interactions within matter and does not require bulk fluid motion.

questions.q: A heat engine primarily converts:
options: Heat input partly into work while rejecting remaining heat
All work into heat with no other interaction
questions.answer: Heat input partly into work while rejecting remaining heat
questions.explanation: A heat engine operates cyclically, receiving heat from a high-temperature source, producing net work and rejecting heat to a lower-temperature sink.

questions.q: Thermal efficiency of a heat engine is defined as:
options: Net work output divided by heat input
Heat rejected divided by work output
Work input divided by heat rejected
questions.answer: Net work output divided by heat input
questions.explanation: Thermal efficiency is η = W_net,out/Q_in for a heat engine.

questions.q: The main purpose of a refrigerator is to:
options: Remove heat from a low-temperature region using work input
Produce work from a single heat reservoir
Increase the temperature of the refrigerated space
questions.answer: Remove heat from a low-temperature region using work input
questions.explanation: A refrigerator uses work input to transfer heat from a low-temperature space to a higher-temperature sink.

questions.q: The coefficient of performance of a refrigerator is:
questions.answer: Q_L/W_net,in
questions.explanation: COP_R is the desired refrigeration effect divided by the required work input.

questions.q: A heat pump is primarily used to:
options: Deliver heat to a high-temperature space using work input
Remove heat from a cold space without work
Convert all heat input into work
questions.answer: Deliver heat to a high-temperature space using work input
questions.explanation: A heat pump transfers heat to the heated space, using work input to drive the process.

questions.q: For the same operating conditions, the relationship between heat-pump and refrigerator COP is:
questions.answer: COP_HP = COP_R + 1
questions.explanation: Because Q_H = Q_L + W_in, COP_HP = Q_H/W_in = COP_R + 1.

questions.q: In a vapour-compression refrigeration cycle, the compressor primarily:
options: Raises the pressure of the refrigerant vapour
Rejects all heat to the room
Absorbs heat from the refrigerated space
questions.answer: Raises the pressure of the refrigerant vapour
questions.explanation: The compressor receives low-pressure vapour and compresses it to a higher-pressure state before condensation.

questions.q: In a vapour-compression refrigeration cycle, the condenser primarily:
options: Rejects heat from the high-pressure refrigerant to the surroundings
Adds work directly to the refrigerant
Absorbs heat from the refrigerated space
questions.answer: Rejects heat from the high-pressure refrigerant to the surroundings
questions.explanation: The condenser removes heat from the high-pressure refrigerant and converts it toward the liquid state.

questions.q: The expansion device in a vapour-compression refrigeration system primarily:
options: Produces a pressure drop before the evaporator
Adds shaft work to the refrigerant
questions.answer: Produces a pressure drop before the evaporator
questions.explanation: The expansion device reduces refrigerant pressure, preparing it for heat absorption in the evaporator.

questions.q: The evaporator in a vapour-compression refrigeration system primarily:
options: Absorbs heat from the refrigerated space
Rejects heat to the surroundings only
questions.answer: Absorbs heat from the refrigerated space
questions.explanation: Low-pressure refrigerant in the evaporator absorbs heat from the space or product being cooled.

questions.q: Which sequence correctly represents the basic vapour-compression refrigeration cycle?
questions.answer: Compressor → condenser → expansion device → evaporator
questions.explanation: The basic cycle proceeds through compression, heat rejection in the condenser, expansion, and heat absorption in the evaporator.

questions.q: HVAC systems combine functions associated with:
questions.answer: Heating, ventilation and air conditioning
questions.explanation: HVAC stands for Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning and deals with thermal comfort and indoor air conditions.
